open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct, or refute by a specific encoded experiment, a finite shared-trace recession library satisfying canonical-section preservation, safety of every positive-weight candidate, simultaneous-collar compatibility, translated-uniform tails, and an input-computable refinement schedule with vanishing accumulated error.
open_obligations.obstruction: The available active-set geometry controls only forward motion from a fixed mean. It does not prove that canonical sections throughout protected stars preserve every active semantic region and the separated-risk set. Equality of shared mesh vertices on a geometric face does not control the actual face--cone candidates throughout simultaneous collar supports. No translated-uniform guard and normal-base tail bound or explicit refinement-count recurrence has been derived. Hence the standing assumptions currently support neither an affirmative construction nor a negative encoded-experiment witness.
open_obligations.attempted: The prior construction used one smoothed ancestor, one common rational simplicial fan, common raywise Foelner factors, and shared finite-element face variables. This gives path-independent operators and explicit translation-boundary ratios. The proposed collar induction is circular if its traces are defined from the already-glued rule, while constant lower-skeleton extension can assign positive weight to an unsafe candidate. Per-cell bounds also cannot be summed without controlling the growing refinement count. In accordance with the directive after this barrier was isolated, no further generic averaging reroll was used.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Starting from the single ancestor \(q_s=K*\phi_{s^2\Sigma}\), \(\mathrm{lem:common\mbox{-}ray\mbox{-}folner\mbox{-}coherence}\) proves that, for every face inclusion \(\tau\preceq\sigma\),
\[
q_{\sigma,L}
=
\left(
\prod_{\varrho\in\mathscr R(\sigma)\setminus\mathscr R(\tau)}
\mathsf A_{\varrho,L}
\right)q_{\tau,L},
\]
independently of the incidence path, together with the bounds
\[
\left\|q_{\sigma,L}(w+a\varrho)-q_{\sigma,L}(w)\right\|_1
\leq 2\min\{1,a/L\}
\]
and
\[
\left|F^f_{\sigma,L}(w+a\varrho)-F^f_{\sigma,L}(w)\right|
\leq R_f\min\{1,a/L\}.
\]
The established smoothing, one-chart averaging, and weighted path results separately give
\[
R_f\min\{1,s^2\sqrt{d/8}\},
\qquad
\frac{R_fk}{T\sqrt{2\pi}},
\qquad
\sum_e\Gamma_{C,e}^f+\frac{R_f}{2}\omega(h)
\]
for each fixed finite library. These identities certify path-independent transitions and the stated componentwise errors only. They do not prove simultaneous safety on collar supports, tails uniform over translated means, or a refinement-count schedule whose accumulated ledger vanishes.

prose_updates.tldr: The unconditional contribution consists of three proved pieces: common-ray Foelner operators are path-independent and have explicit translation-boundary ratios; Carter's bounded-ratio kernels give fixed-base compact multinomial transfer with separately displayed semantic, covariance, and \(C_{2/\kappa}m\log(m)/\sqrt n\) charges; and compact exhaustion gives a global minimax lower limit together with two-sided convergence on diagonally selected expanding lawful windows, but no global upper limit. Replayable moving-offset transfer and CertGluePFL termination remain conditional on an affirmative resolution of the effective-compatible-density question or on a separately proved sufficient compatibility package.

project_justification.gap: Carter's bounded-ratio comparison controls fixed positive-cell multinomial experiments on compact parameter sets, but it neither supplies finite recession libraries nor controls a seam escaping every compact set. Moving offsets additionally require compact-offset arrangement stability and separately supplied envelopes for replayable accounting. At recession, common-ray commutativity does not control the Gaussian-weighted discrepancy between every incident candidate on simultaneous collars. Effective compatible density therefore remains the question of deriving canonical-section safety, positive-weight candidate safety, translated-uniform tails, and an input-computable refinement schedule with vanishing total ledger.
project_justification.niche: Finite-label partial-identification inference combines discontinuous completed labels, intersecting unbounded recession faces, and a global honesty constraint. Equality on a geometric face does not control all candidates mixed on nearby simultaneous collars, while compact local asymptotics cannot detect a hard seam escaping to infinity. The proved compact/windowed theory and the unanswered compatibility-density question at unbounded recession seams are therefore mathematically distinct.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves common-ray operator coherence, Carter-based fixed-base compact transfer with separate semantic and covariance terms, a global minimax lower limit, and two-sided convergence on diagonally selected expanding lawful windows. It does not prove global effective compatible density. The corresponding open-ended question lists the five certificates still required. Replayable moving-offset rules and CertGluePFL termination are asserted only under an affirmative answer or a separately proved sufficient compatibility package.

prose_updates.related_work: Carter (2002, Theorem 1 and Sections 2--6) supplies the bounded-ratio comparison between fixed positive-cell multinomial experiments and their matched multivariate normal experiments through parameter-independent kernels. The present paper separately accounts for score maps, covariance replacement, completed-affine-arrangement stability, moving offsets, and diagonally selected expanding lawful windows. Blanco, Flores, and Flores-Lagunes (2013, Assumptions A--B and Proposition 1) motivate an always-employed wage comparison; the asserted embedding is restricted to the singleton-covariate, known rational assignment-floor, perfect-compliance, monotone-employment, finite-wage-grid submodel with positive always-employed mass, and gives neither unrestricted-class inclusion nor automatic sharpness transfer. Day and Markov--Kakutani invariant-mean theory and Namioka's 1964 Foelner conditions concern a single amenable commuting action and supply neither an input-computable modulus nor semantic coverage, separated-risk safety, translated-tail control, or branching-refinement complexity.
prose_updates.interpretation: The Gaussian experiment is the valid local decision target on each fixed lawful direction window. Carter's comparison gives unconditional qualitative fixed-compact and moving-offset transfer once the respective compact hypotheses hold; finite replayable Gaussian-rule construction remains conditional on effective compatible density or another sufficient compatibility package, and numerical replayability also requires separately supplied effective error envelopes. Compact exhaustion gives a global minimax lower limit and two-sided convergence only along diagonally selected expanding lawful windows; it gives neither a computable window selection nor a global upper limit. The common-ray library is an algebraically coherent recession representation, not a compatibility-density theorem.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Effective compatible density is unresolved under the standing assumptions. One unproved obligation is to show that every canonical chart section remains in each required \(D_v\), \(H_r\), and declared chart-neighborhood incidence region. The remaining obligations are safety of every positive-weight candidate; exact overlap traces or a valid Gaussian-weighted face-cone discrepancy bound on simultaneous supports; translated-uniform guard and normal-base tails; and computed refinement counts \(N_j\) with schedules \(L_j,B_j,\delta_j\) for which every accumulated error vanishes and \(N_j/L_j\) tends to zero. No refinement-independent ledger constant is assumed. The four-label milliscale certificate and unconditional global CertGluePFL termination therefore remain unresolved.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The causal target is the same-law joint identified set and is only contained in the product of coordinatewise sharp endpoint intervals; no Cartesian joint sharpness is claimed. Carter-backed sampled-data conclusions are fixed-compact or expanding-window statements. Compact exhaustion proves a global lower limit and two-sided windowed convergence, but neither a global limsup nor a globally honest unbounded sampled-data primal. The paper proves common-ray operator identities, Gaussian smoothing, one-chart averaging, and the weighted telescoping inequality for any already specified finite family with certified edge discrepancies. It does not prove existence of finite families whose total compatibility ledger vanishes. Effective compatible density remains an open-ended question, and CertGluePFL termination and replayable global Gaussian certification remain conditional.

statement_notes.justification: This question isolates the exact effective geometric package still needed to turn coherent recession operators into a finite globally honest search space.
statement_notes.gap: The standing assumptions do not yet yield simultaneous canonical-section safety, collar compatibility, translated-uniform tails, or a refinement schedule whose total ledger vanishes.
statement_notes.consumer: Only an affirmative answer, or a separately proved sufficient compatibility package, can supply the finite Gaussian-rule premise needed by conditional CertGluePFL termination and replayable moving-offset certification.

proofs.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: parameter-independent Le Cam transfer, an affine score map, Gaussian Hellinger comparison, and finite-arrangement stability.}

Let
\[
D_n=\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(0)\},\qquad
I_n=B'D_n^{-1}B,\qquad \Sigma_n=I_n^{-1}.
\tag{1}
\]
The inverses in (1) exist for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Indeed, \(p_n(0)=p_0\), \(\min_j(p_0)_j\ge\kappa>0\) by \(\text{ass:multinomial-interior}\), and \(B\) has column rank \(d\); hence for every nonzero \(z\in\mathbb R^d\),
\[
z'I_nz=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\frac{\{(Bz)_j\}^2}{(p_0)_j}>0.
\tag{2}
\]
Thus \(I_n\succ0\), and in the fixed-base case \(I_n=I_0\) and \(\Sigma_n=\Sigma_0\).

By \(\text{prop:carter-fixed-m-positive-cell}\), Carter's two parameter-independent Markov kernels apply uniformly to \(\{p_n(u):u\in C\}\), with total-variation error
\[
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Car},n}
=C_{2/\kappa}\frac{m\log m}{\sqrt n}.
\tag{3}
\]
For the matched normal count vector \(Y_n\), apply the fixed affine score map
\[
S_n(Y_n)=\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}
\frac{Y_n-np_n(0)}{\sqrt n}.
\tag{4}
\]
At parameter \(u\), (4) is Gaussian with mean and covariance
\[
\mu_n(u)=\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}\sqrt n\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\},
\tag{5}
\]
\[
V_n(u)=\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}
\left[\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(u)\}-p_n(u)p_n(u)'\right]
D_n^{-1}B\Sigma_n.
\tag{6}
\]
Because \(\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}B=I_d\), the definition of \(d_n(C)\) gives
\[
\sup_{u\in C}\|\mu_n(u)-u\|_2
\le \|\Sigma_nB'D_n^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}d_n(C).
\tag{7}
\]
The compact expansion assumption implies \(d_n(C)\to0\).  Base convergence and \(\text{lem:compact-moving-remainder-covariance}\) imply
\[
\sup_{u\in C}\|V_n(u)-\Sigma_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to0.
\tag{8}
\]

For positive definite \(V\), define
\[
\mathsf H^2(\mu,V;u,\Sigma_0)
=2-2\frac{|V|^{1/4}|\Sigma_0|^{1/4}}
{|(V+\Sigma_0)/2|^{1/2}}
\exp\left[-\frac18(\mu-u)'
\{(V+\Sigma_0)/2\}^{-1}(\mu-u)\right].
\tag{9}
\]
Direct completion of the square in the product of the two Gaussian densities shows that the second term in (9) is twice their Hellinger affinity.  The inequality between total variation and Hellinger distance therefore yields the explicit enclosure
\[
\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)
=\sup_{u\in C}\min\{1,
\mathsf H(\mu_n(u),V_n(u);u,\Sigma_0)\}.
\tag{10}
\]
Equations (7)--(8), compactness of \(C\), and eventual uniform positive definiteness imply
\(\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\to0\).

At the fixed base, the moving-slack identity has zero offset.  Apply \(\text{lem:finite-completed-arrangement-stability}\) to the finite completed arrangement.  If a finite-sample semantic label is active at \(u\in C\), there is an incident zero-offset Gaussian mean \(\bar u\) with
\[
\|u-\bar u\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}
\le H_Cx_n(C),
\qquad x_n(C)=d_n(C)+\delta_n(C).
\tag{11}
\]
The same lemma's directed Hausdorff conclusion changes every distance to a rival semantic union by at most twice the right side of (11); enlarge the finitely enumerated \(H_C\) once to absorb this factor and the equal-covariance Gaussian translation constant.  Equality faces lose no coverage constraint because every incident completion contains the equality face.

It remains to bound the means for which a perturbed active sign can differ.  Since \(a_j\ne0\) and \(\Sigma_0\succ0\),
\(a_j'\Sigma_0a_j>0\).  For \(W_0\sim N_d(h,\Sigma_0)\), the scalar \(a_j'W_0\) has a density bounded by
\(\{2\pi a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{-1/2}\), uniformly in \(h\).  Hence, for \(s\ge0\),
\[
\Pr_h\{|a_j'W_0|\le s\}
\le \min\left\{1,
\frac{2s}{\sqrt{2\pi}\{a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{1/2}}
\right\}.
\tag{12}
\]
The union bound and the definition of \(\mathfrak b_0\) give
\[
\mathfrak b_0(s)\le A_0s,
\qquad
A_0=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}
\frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}\{a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{1/2}}.
\tag{13}
\]
Both sides of (13) are zero when the active list is empty.

The previously displayed fixed-stratum bound has geometric term
\(H_Cx+\mathbf 1\{x>\tau\}\) and boundary term \(\mathfrak b_0(\tau)\).  Set \(x=x_n(C)\) and \(\tau=x_n(C)\).  The strict indicator is then zero, and (13) bounds the boundary term by \(A_0x_n(C)\).  Finally, apply \(\text{lem:bounded-semantic-transfer-by-tv}\) first to Carter's kernel and then to the Gaussian comparison (10), once with \(\mathbf 1\{v\in A\}\in[0,1]\) and once with \(\ell_0(A)\in[0,1]\).  Combining (3), (10)--(13) yields
\[
\mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{lin}}(C)
\le C_{2/\kappa}\frac{m\log m}{\sqrt n}
+(H_C+A_0)x_n(C)+\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C).
\tag{14}
\]
The local expansion and \(\text{lem:compact-moving-remainder-covariance}\) give \(x_n(C)\to0\), so every term in (14) vanishes.  Equation (14) displays, rather than suppresses, the two terms for which no root-\(n\) rate is assumed.

\textbf{Technique: compatible affine-offset lifting followed by the unconditional Carter--geometry lemma; effectivity is separated from qualitative convergence.}

Let \(A_\Psi\) have rows \(\alpha_j'\), \(j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}\), and write
\(L_{\mathrm{ASC}}=\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\).  Since every active cut has \(\psi_j(p_0)=0\),
\[
c_n=A_\Psi\sqrt n\{p_n(0)-p_0\}.
\tag{21}
\]
The local-family affine-hull assumption places the vector inside braces in \(L_{\mathrm{ASC}}\).  By the definition of \(\mathcal K_0\),
\[
c_n\in\mathcal K_0\qquad\text{for every }n.
\tag{22}
\]
The effective moving-offset encoding assumption supplies the declared rational \(\widehat c_n\) for each chosen rational \(\xi_n>0\).  Because \(c_n\to c\), \(\xi_n\to0\), and
\(\|\widehat c_n-c_n\|_\infty\le\xi_n\), there is a closed bounded set \(C_c\subset\mathcal K_0\) containing both sequences after finitely many indices.  In finite dimension this set is compact.  This discharges, rather than silently assumes, the compact-offset premise of \(\text{lem:moving-offset-carter-geometry}\), and fixes
\[
H_C=H(C,C_c)<\infty.
\tag{23}
\]

The local expansion and \(\text{lem:compact-moving-remainder-covariance}\) give
\[
d_n(C)\to0,
\qquad \delta_n(C)\to0,
\qquad \operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\to0.
\tag{24}
\]
Therefore \(\chi_n(C)=d_n(C)+\delta_n(C)+\xi_n\to0\).  Apply \(\text{lem:moving-offset-carter-geometry}\) first with an arbitrary supplied bound \(\overline\chi_n(C)\ge\chi_n(C)\).  It yields the displayed \(\Delta_n(C)\).  In particular the mathematical choice
\(\overline\chi_n(C)=\chi_n(C)\) is valid without being computable, and (23)--(24) imply \(\Delta_n(C)\to0\).  This proves the unconditional qualitative statistical comparison for every supplied Gaussian rule.

We next verify that the rule's offset experiment is legitimate.  Since \(\widehat c_n\in\mathcal K_0\cap\mathbb Q^{|\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}|}\), rational linear algebra gives a rational \(z_n\in L_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) satisfying
\(A_\Psi z_n=\widehat c_n\).  For each fixed \(u\), relative interiority and tangent-image compatibility give, for all sufficiently small positive \(t\),
\[
p_0+t(z_n+Bu)\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}.
\tag{25}
\]
The compatible completed branch at (25) has active signs
\[
\operatorname{sgn}\{\alpha_j'(z_n+Bu)\}
=\operatorname{sgn}(\widehat c_{n,j}+a_j'u),
\tag{26}
\]
and a zero sign belongs to every incident completion.  Hence the offset semantic cells cover \(\mathbb R^d\).

For nonemptiness of the separated domain, take a strict chamber direction of the homogeneous completed fan.  Along a sufficiently large multiple of that direction the fixed offset in (26) is dominated by the strict homogeneous slacks.  For each rival polyhedral component there is a nonzero rational row \(a'\) whose gap is \(t\gamma+O(1)\), \(\gamma>0\).  Every point \(g\) in that rival satisfies
\[
t\gamma+O(1)\le a'(ty-g)
\le\|a\|_{\Sigma_0}\|ty-g\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}.
\tag{27}
\]
The divisor \(\|a\|_{\Sigma_0}\) is positive because \(a\ne0\) and \(\Sigma_0\succ0\).  Taking the infimum over \(g\) and then the minimum over finitely many rivals shows that the separation eventually exceeds \(r_0\).  If the active list is empty, the unique global semantic label gives the conclusion directly.  Thus the offset object has a complete cover, rational encoding, positive definite covariance, and nonempty separated domain; it belongs to \(\mathfrak E\).

The preceding argument constructs no finite Gaussian rule.  If the affirmative conclusion specified in \(\text{oeq:effective-compatible-density}\), or a separately proved sufficient compatibility package, is supplied, then the conditional \(\text{thm:certglue-termination}\) produces such a finite replayable rule and its outward Gaussian ledger.  Composing it with Carter's forward kernel adds \(\Delta_n(C)\) to the certified chart, tail, integration, and rounding charges.  The standing effective moving-remainder and offset-encoding assumptions provide effective bounds only for \(\delta_n(C)\) and \(\xi_n\).  To turn the complete comparison charge into a replayable numerical receipt one must additionally supply effective rational upper enclosures for \(d_n(C)\) and \(\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\).  This is an input condition for replayability, not a scientific assumption and not a consequence of effective compatible density.  Every supremum above is restricted to \(C\), so no unbounded-region conclusion follows.

\textbf{Technique: diagonal compact exhaustion, finite-support dual transfer, and exact windowwise repair.}

Write \(B_k=\{u:\|u\|_2\le k\}\).  Fix \(k\).  By \(\text{lem:compact-causal-domain}\), the relative-interior, affine-hull, base-convergence, and compact local-expansion premises imply
\[
B_k\subseteq\mathcal U_n
\tag{28}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  By \(\text{prop:carter-fixed-m-positive-cell}\),
\[
\min_{u\in B_k}\min_{j\in\mathcal J}p_{n,j}(u)\ge\kappa/2
\tag{29}
\]
eventually.  Zero-offset centering, the local expansion, and \(\text{lem:compact-moving-remainder-covariance}\) show that every comparison term in \(\mathscr E_n(\ell)\) tends to zero for each fixed \(\ell\le k\).  There are finitely many such \(\ell\), so (28)--(29) and
\(\mathscr E_n(\ell)\le1/\ell\) hold simultaneously for every \(1\le\ell\le k\) once \(n\) is large enough.  The diagonal definition then gives \(R_n^{\diamond}\ge k\), whence
\[
R_n^{\diamond}\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{30}
\]
This is an existence argument based on eventual inequalities.  It supplies no algorithm for deciding those eventual indices or the compact suprema.

At \(k=R_n^{\diamond}\), the defining inequalities bound the Carter, covariance, offset, boundary, and finite-arrangement errors on the selected window by a deterministic number \(\rho_n\to0\).  The convergence follows because the accepted index tends to infinity by (30), while the diagonal tolerance at that index tends to zero.  This is the only moving-window comparison used below.

Let \(L<M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\).  By \(\text{thm:attainment-atomic-duality}\), there is a finite atomic Gaussian dual certificate \(\mu\) of value greater than \(L\).  Its finite support lies in some \(B_k\).  Zero-offset centering and \(\text{lem:finite-completed-arrangement-stability}\) realize each coverage atom in \(D_v^0\) by an atom in \(D_{n,v}\cap B_{k+1}\) at Mahalanobis distance tending to zero.  An equality-face atom is realized separately for each constraint role, and the completed convention retains its incident label.

For a risk atom \(h\in H_{r_0}\), the realization may be kept in \(H_{n,r_0}\).  If \(r_0>0\), the zero-offset cells are cones and distance to every rival cone is positively homogeneous.  Replace \(h\) by \((1+t_n)h\), where \(t_n\downarrow0\) slowly enough that the gained distance margin exceeds twice the directed Hausdorff error.  Arrangement stability then gives a finite-sample atom whose distance from every rival union is at least \(r_0\).  If \(r_0=0\), uniqueness of the label at \(h\) and closedness of the finite rival union give a strictly positive atom-specific distance, so the same conclusion holds once the arrangement error is smaller than half that distance.  By (30), every finite collection of these atoms lies in \(B_{R_n^{\diamond}}\) eventually.

Apply Carter's reverse parameter-independent kernel to an arbitrary window-honest multinomial rule, followed by the score and covariance maps.  By \(\text{lem:bounded-semantic-transfer-by-tv}\), the error in the finite dual objective is at most \(A_\mu\rho_n\), where \(A_\mu<\infty\) is the sum of the absolute dual coefficients.  Weak duality yields
\[
M_n^{\diamond}\ge L-A_\mu\rho_n.
\tag{31}
\]
First let \(n\to\infty\) and then \(L\uparrow M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\) to obtain
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n^{\diamond}
\ge M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
\tag{32}
\]

For the opposite inequality, fix \(a>0\).  Attainment supplies a measurable \(K^a\in\mathcal C_{\eta_0}\) satisfying
\[
\sup_{h\in H_{r_0}}E_h\ell_0\{K^a(W_0)\}
\le M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)+a.
\tag{33}
\]
Carter's forward kernel applies to every measurable randomized rule, so no finite representation is needed.  On \(B_{R_n^{\diamond}}\), the diagonal score, covariance, completed-arrangement, and boundary comparisons show that the transferred rule has coverage at least \(1-\eta_0-\rho_n\) and separated risk at most
\[
M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)+a+\rho_n.
\tag{34}
\]
At the boundary of \(H_{r_0}\), (34) follows from the same explicit restoration used for the dual atoms.  For \(r_0>0\), radial dilation restores a deficit \(\gamma<r_0/2\) at displacement at most \(2R_n^{\diamond}\gamma/r_0\), a term included before the diagonal test accepts the window.  For \(r_0=0\), finite active-set chamber approximation and Gaussian-shift continuity supply the corresponding term.  Equality faces retain every coverage label.

Apply \(\text{lem:exact-coverage-repair}\) with coverage and risk restricted to the selected window.  With
\[
q_n=\frac{\rho_n}{\eta_0+\rho_n},
\tag{35}
\]
the denominator is positive because \(\eta_0>0\), and
\[
(1-q_n)(1-\eta_0-\rho_n)+q_n=1-\eta_0.
\tag{36}
\]
Since \(0\le\ell_0\le1\), the repaired rule belongs to the window-honest class and
\[
M_n^{\diamond}
\le M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)+a+\rho_n
+\frac{\rho_n}{\eta_0+\rho_n}.
\tag{37}
\]
Let \(n\to\infty\), then \(a\downarrow0\), and combine (32) and (37):
\[
M_n^{\diamond}\longrightarrow M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
\tag{38}
\]

The globally honest class is contained in the window-honest class, and the global risk supremum is over a superset of the window risk domain.  Directly from the definitions,
\[
M_n\ge M_n^{\diamond}.
\tag{39}
\]
Equations (38)--(39) prove
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n
\ge M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
\tag{40}
\]

If the affirmative effective-compatible-density conclusion, or a separate sufficient package, is supplied, the abstract \(K^a\) in (33) may be replaced by a CertGluePFL finite receipt; provided the finite-window comparison enclosures are also supplied, its Carter transfer and repair (35) are replayable.  This conditional statement does not make the diagonal selection in (30) computable.  Finally, \(\text{lem:escaping-boundary-kill}\) gives two arrays identical on every fixed compact but with different global upper behavior.  It rules out a global \(\limsup\) conclusion from the compact-uniform premises.

\textbf{Technique: effective dovetailing of sound primal and dual semidecisions.}

This proof begins with the additional premise in the statement; it does not derive that premise from the standing assumptions.  The exact part of the affirmative effective-compatible-density conclusion needed here is a computable sequence \(\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)\downarrow0\) and enumerable finite records \(Q_j(K)\in\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,j}\) such that, for every \(K\in\mathcal C_\eta\), the record eventually produced for index \(j\) has a verifiable outward ledger satisfying
\[
\begin{split}
c\{Q_j(K)\}&\ge1-\eta-\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j),\\
r\{Q_j(K)\}&\le R_r(K)+D\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j),\\
\rho_{\mathrm{led}}\{Q_j(K)\}&\le\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j).
\end{split}
\tag{41}
\]
Here \(c(Q)\) is the infimum of semantic-label coverage and \(r(Q)\) is the supremum of separated diameter risk.  The premise includes finite certificates for canonical-section preservation, safety of every positive-weight candidate, collar discrepancy, translated tails, and refinement counts.  A separately proved sufficient compatibility package is admissible precisely when it supplies (41) with the same verifiability and computability properties.

At stage \(s\), enumerate the finitely many indices \(j\le s\), codes of records in \(\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,j}\) of length at most \(s\), rational incidence forests, semantic projections, atomic action probabilities, and integration and rounding precisions among the first \(s\) choices.  The checks in \(\text{def:weighted-error-ledger}\) return rational outward enclosures
\[
c^-_{Q,s}\le c(Q),
\qquad r(Q)\le r^+_{Q,s}.
\tag{42}
\]
A record is accepted only after every rational incidence, projection, protected-neighborhood, covariance, Gaussian-tail, quadrature, and rounding check needed for (42) has passed.  Thus acceptance uses no uncertified floating-point sign.

After intersecting the coverage enclosure with \([0,1]\), set
\[
\rho_{Q,s}=\max\{0,1-\eta-c^-_{Q,s}\},
\qquad q_{Q,s}=\frac{\rho_{Q,s}}{\eta+\rho_{Q,s}}.
\tag{43}
\]
Because \(0<\eta<1/2\) and \(0\le c^-_{Q,s}\le1\),
\[
0\le\rho_{Q,s}\le1-\eta<1,
\qquad \eta+\rho_{Q,s}>0.
\tag{44}
\]
Thus the division in (43) is valid, and (42)--(43) imply
\(c(Q)\ge1-\eta-\rho_{Q,s}\).  By \(\text{lem:exact-coverage-repair}\), the archived rule
\(Q^+=\operatorname{Repair}_{\eta,\rho_{Q,s}}(Q)\) is globally honest and
\[
M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)
\le R_r(Q^+)
\le r^+_{Q,s}+Dq_{Q,s}.
\tag{45}
\]
Outward interval arithmetic produces a rational \(U_{Q,s}\) no smaller than the last expression in (45).

In parallel, enumerate the finite atomic dual records from \(\text{thm:attainment-atomic-duality}\), with rational weights and rational real-algebraic support encodings.  Membership in a finite union \(D_v\) and membership in \(H_r\) reduce to finitely many exact polynomial-sign, rational polyhedral, and convex quadratic-distance tests.  Refine each feasible record's Gaussian integrals until a rational lower endpoint \(l^-_{\nu,s}\) is obtained.  Every such endpoint is a valid lower certificate.  Put
\[
L_s=\max_{\nu\text{ processed by }s}l^-_{\nu,s},
\qquad
U_s=\min_{Q\text{ accepted by }s}U_{Q,s},
\tag{46}
\]
leaving an endpoint undefined if its finite collection is empty.  Weak duality and (45) imply, whenever both are defined,
\[
L_s\le M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\le U_s.
\tag{47}
\]

Each fixed stage terminates.  Its enumerated collections are finite, its geometry checks are finite exact rational or real-algebraic programs, and each requested Gaussian enclosure is obtained on a rational box by interval subdivision, with the complement bounded by an explicit Gaussian tail.  Accepted finite records carry moduli on the box, so the subdivision error tends to zero; the tail tends to zero as the box expands.  Every positive requested enclosure width is therefore reached after finitely many operations.

It remains to prove that the stopping test is eventually met.  By \(\text{thm:attainment-atomic-duality}\), there is \(K^*\in\mathcal C_\eta\) with
\[
R_r(K^*)=M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r).
\tag{48}
\]
Apply (41) to \(K^*\).  For any rational \(\zeta>0\), sufficiently fine outward evaluation of its finite record gives
\[
c^-_{Q_j(K^*),s}\ge c\{Q_j(K^*)\}-\zeta,
\qquad
r^+_{Q_j(K^*),s}\le r\{Q_j(K^*)\}+\zeta.
\tag{49}
\]
Equations (41), (43), and (49) imply
\[
\rho_{Q_j(K^*),s}\le\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+\zeta.
\tag{50}
\]
Combining (41), (45), and (48)--(50), and assigning at most another \(\zeta\) to the final outward rounding, gives
\[
U_s\le M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)
+D\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+2\zeta
+\frac{D\{\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+\zeta\}}
{\eta+\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+\zeta}.
\tag{51}
\]
The denominator is positive by \(\eta>0\).  First increase \(j\), then decrease \(\zeta\); the right side tends to \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\).  The atomic-duality theorem also gives an enumerated increasing sequence of lower certificates converging to the same value.  Hence
\[
L_s\uparrow M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r),
\qquad \limsup_{s\to\infty}U_s\le M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r).
\tag{52}
\]
Together with (47), (52) proves that some finite stage satisfies \(U_s-L_s\le\varepsilon\).

For the cost receipt, let \(a_i(\mathfrak G,s)\) be the number of operations of type
\(i\in\{\mathrm{glue},\mathrm{cut},\mathrm{Gauss},\mathrm{LP}\}\) at stage \(s\), and let \(b(\mathfrak G,s)\) be the largest bit length encountered there.  Define by primitive recursion
\[
\begin{aligned}
C_i(0)&=a_i(\mathfrak G,0),&
C_i(s+1)&=C_i(s)+a_i(\mathfrak G,s+1),\\
B(0)&=b(\mathfrak G,0),&
B(s+1)&=\max\{B(s),b(\mathfrak G,s+1)\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{53}
\]
Let
\[
s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)
=\min\{s:L_s,U_s\text{ are defined and }U_s-L_s\le\varepsilon\}.
\tag{54}
\]
The test in (54) is rational, and (52) proves that its sequential search halts.  Therefore \(s_*\) is total recursive under the displayed conditional premise.  Set
\[
N_i(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)=C_i\{s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\},
\quad
i\in\{\mathrm{glue},\mathrm{cut},\mathrm{Gauss},\mathrm{LP}\},
\tag{55}
\]
\[
\operatorname{Bit}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)
=B\{s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\}.
\tag{56}
\]
Archive at stage \(s_*\) the repaired primal attaining the finite minimum and the atomic dual attaining the finite maximum in (46).  Equations (47), (54)--(56) give the asserted gap, exact honesty, termination, and five-part receipt.  All conclusions remain conditional on (41).

\textbf{Technique: composition of exact finite-fiber identification, rational tangent geometry, compact experiment comparison, and the restricted published-model embedding.}

Let \(P_0\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) and \(p_0=p(P_0)\).  The assignment, support, randomization, three consistency conditions, no-defiers, complier-conditional selection monotonicity, and aggregate target-positivity conditions are precisely the separately declared restrictions defining \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\).  In particular,
\[
M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\ge m_*>0,
\tag{57}
\]
so the conditional causal quantiles have a positive denominator.

By \(\text{thm:causal-label-polyhedralization}\), the observed-cell contrasts identify the selected-complier submeasures, and the finite response-type fiber is exactly the compatible full-law fiber.  For every fixed \(t\in\mathcal T\), \(\text{prop:lower-endpoint-attainment}\) and \(\text{prop:upper-endpoint-attainment}\) give same-law witnesses
\[
Q_{1,P_t^-(p_0)}(t)-Q_{0,P_t^-(p_0)}(t)
=\underline\Delta(t;p_0),
\tag{58}
\]
\[
Q_{1,P_t^+(p_0)}(t)-Q_{0,P_t^+(p_0)}(t)
=\overline\Delta(t;p_0).
\tag{59}
\]
For any one \(P\in\mathcal F(p_0)\), the definitions of infimum and supremum yield
\[
\underline\Delta(t;p_0)
\le Q_{1,P}(t)-Q_{0,P}(t)
\le\overline\Delta(t;p_0).
\tag{60}
\]
Taking all \(t\) and all compatible \(P\) proves the outer bound
\[
\Theta_{\mathrm{ASC}}(p_0)
\subseteq\prod_{t\in\mathcal T}
[\underline\Delta(t;p_0),\overline\Delta(t;p_0)].
\tag{61}
\]
The witnesses in (58)--(59) may depend on both \(t\) and the endpoint, so (61) is not a Cartesian sharpness statement.

Under relative interiority and tangent-image compatibility, \(\text{prop:tangent-fan-global-cover}\) proves
\(\bigcup_{v\in V}D_v^0=\mathbb R^d\), with equality faces included in every incident label.  Since \(B\) has column rank \(d\) and \((p_0)_j\ge\kappa>0\), for nonzero \(z\),
\[
z'I_0z=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}
\frac{\{(Bz)_j\}^2}{(p_0)_j}>0.
\tag{62}
\]
Thus \(I_0\succ0\) and \(\Sigma_0=I_0^{-1}\succ0\).  Rational \(p_0\) and \(B\) give rational \(\Sigma_0\).  The violated-row certificate in \(\text{prop:job-corps-radius-nonempty}\) proves \(H_{r_0}\ne\varnothing\).  These are exactly the cover, covariance, rational-encoding, and separated-domain conditions for
\[
\mathfrak G_0\in\mathfrak E.
\tag{63}
\]

The proved \(\text{thm:fixed-stratum-transfer}\) gives the compact linear modulus
\[
C_{2/\kappa}\frac{|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|}{\sqrt n}
+(H_C+A_0)x_n(C)+\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C),
\tag{64}
\]
without assigning a root-\(n\) rate to the last two terms.  The proved \(\text{lem:moving-offset-carter-geometry}\) and \(\text{thm:moving-offset-transfer}\) give, for every supplied Gaussian rule on a fixed compact \(C\),
\[
C_{2/\kappa}\frac{|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|}{\sqrt n}
+\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)
+(H_C+2A_0)\overline\chi_n(C).
\tag{65}
\]
The sequences of actual and rationalized offsets lie in one fixed compact offset set because \(c_n\to c\) and \(\|\widehat c_n-c_n\|_\infty\to0\).  Hence the same finite \(H_C\) applies in (65).  The choice \(\overline\chi_n=\chi_n\) proves qualitative convergence.  A replayable finite Gaussian rule in (65) is available only under the affirmative effective-compatible-density conclusion or another sufficient package, and effective rational bounds for \(d_n(C)\) and \(\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\) must separately be supplied for replayable comparison accounting.

Under zero-offset centering, \(\text{thm:compact-exhaustion-transfer}\) gives the diagonally selected window conclusions
\[
M_n^{\diamond}\longrightarrow M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0),
\qquad
\liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n
\ge M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
\tag{66}
\]
Its diagonal argument proves existence of expanding lawful windows, not an algorithm for selecting them.

Finally, \(\text{prop:bffl-discrete-perfect-compliance-embedding}\) records the precise comparison with Blanco, Flores, and Flores-Lagunes.  On its singleton-\(\mathcal X\) restriction, perfect compliance gives
\[
D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)>D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)\quad\text{almost surely},
\tag{67}
\]
and \(s=+1\) turns monotone employment into the declared complier-conditional selection monotonicity.  Therefore
\[
\{D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)>D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0),
S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}=EE,
\qquad M_{\mathrm{ASC}}=P(EE)\ge m_*>0.
\tag{68}
\]
Known rational assignment with \(\bar\pi_z\ge\pi_*\), randomized treatment, and the finite wage-grid restriction supply the remaining declared support and encoding requirements.  Thus this restricted law belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\).  Dropping perfect compliance, singleton support, the common assignment floor, or finite wage support leaves premises unmatched; consequently neither unrestricted class inclusion nor automatic transfer of a published sharpness result follows.

If effective compatible density is affirmatively resolved, conditional CertGluePFL applied to (63) yields the replayable Gaussian certificate; otherwise only the unconditional comparisons (64)--(66) remain.  The witness in \(\text{lem:escaping-boundary-kill}\) rules out deriving a global sampled-data upper limit from these compact premises.  This completes exactly the claimed identification, tangent, compact-transfer, diagonal-window, and conditional-certification conclusions.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix a rational compact polytope \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\).  Let \(c_n,\widehat c_n\in\mathcal K_0\) lie eventually in one fixed compact set \(C_c\subset\mathcal K_0\), suppose \(\|\widehat c_n-c_n\|_\infty\le\xi_n\), and define
\[
\chi_n(C)=d_n(C)+\delta_n(C)+\xi_n,
\qquad
A_0=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}
\frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}\{a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{1/2}}.
\]
For any supplied Gaussian rule in the \(\widehat c_n\)-offset experiment and any supplied upper bound \(\overline\chi_n(C)\ge\chi_n(C)\), the parameter-independent Carter and score transfer has semantic coverage discrepancy and normalized separated-risk discrepancy on \(C\) at most
\[
\Delta_n(C)=C_{2/\kappa}\frac{|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|}{\sqrt n}
+\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)
+\{H_C+2A_0\}\overline\chi_n(C),
\qquad H_C=H(C,C_c).
\]
The upper bound \(\overline\chi_n(C)\) is arbitrary and need not be effective.  If \(\overline\chi_n(C)\to0\), then \(\Delta_n(C)\to0\).  This conclusion constructs no Gaussian rule and invokes no effective-compatible-density premise.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: exact affine-slack coupling, compact-offset finite-arrangement stability, and bounded Gaussian boundary density.}

For every active facet, \(\text{def:moving-slack-system}\) gives the exact identity
\[
\zeta_{n,j}(u)-\{\widehat c_{n,j}+a_j'u\}
=(c_{n,j}-\widehat c_{n,j})+e_{n,j}(u).
\tag{15}
\]
Consequently,
\[
\max_j\sup_{u\in C}
\left|\zeta_{n,j}(u)-\{\widehat c_{n,j}+a_j'u\}\right|
\le\delta_n(C)+\xi_n\le\chi_n(C).
\tag{16}
\]
The hypothesis that \(c_n\) and \(\widehat c_n\) lie in the same fixed compact \(C_c\subset\mathcal K_0\) is now used: it permits invocation of \(\text{lem:finite-completed-arrangement-stability}\) with its single finite constant
\(H_C=H(C,C_c)\).  Together with the centered score displacement \(d_n(C)\), (16) matches every completed semantic label mean and every separated-risk mean to the \(\widehat c_n\)-offset arrangement at Mahalanobis displacement at most
\[
H_C\chi_n(C).
\tag{17}
\]
The lemma's directed Hausdorff part handles rival semantic unions, and its equality convention retains all incident labels.

For each active \(j\), positivity of \(\Sigma_0\) and \(a_j\ne0\) imply \(a_j'\Sigma_0a_j>0\).  The same density calculation as in (12) gives, uniformly over the offset and the Gaussian mean,
\[
\Pr_h\{|c_j+a_j'W_0|\le s\}
\le\min\left\{1,
\frac{2s}{\sqrt{2\pi}\{a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{1/2}}\right\}.
\tag{18}
\]
Thus \(\mathfrak b_0(s)\le A_0s\).  In the moving-boundary comparison take the collar tolerance to be
\(\tau_n=\overline\chi_n(C)\).  Because
\(\chi_n(C)\le\overline\chi_n(C)\), the strict failure indicator
\(\mathbf1\{\chi_n(C)>\tau_n\}\) equals zero, while
\[
\mathfrak b_0\{\tau_n+\chi_n(C)\}
\le\mathfrak b_0\{2\overline\chi_n(C)\}
\le2A_0\overline\chi_n(C).
\tag{19}
\]
Also (17) is at most \(H_C\overline\chi_n(C)\).

By \(\text{prop:carter-fixed-m-positive-cell}\), Carter's parameter-independent kernel contributes
\(C_{2/\kappa}|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|/\sqrt n\) on \(C\).  The affine score-normal replacement contributes \(\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\), and \(\text{lem:bounded-semantic-transfer-by-tv}\) applies both to coverage indicators and to \(\ell_0\in[0,1]\).  Adding these nonnegative charges to (17)--(19) proves
\[
\Delta_n(C)
=C_{2/\kappa}\frac{|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|}{\sqrt n}
+\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)
+(H_C+2A_0)\overline\chi_n(C).
\tag{20}
\]
If \(\overline\chi_n(C)\to0\), compactness of the fixed offset set keeps \(H_C\) fixed, \(\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\to0\) by \(\text{lem:compact-moving-remainder-covariance}\), and the Carter term vanishes.  Hence \(\Delta_n(C)\to0\).

added_lemmas.gap: Its upper bound may be qualitative unless rational envelopes for the centered expansion and covariance replacement are supplied.

added_lemmas.statement: The randomized-treatment, monotone-employment, always-employed model of Blanco, Flores, and Flores-Lagunes embeds in the present causal class only on the following restricted submodel: \(\mathcal X\) is a singleton; the known rational assignment probabilities satisfy \(\bar\pi_z\ge\pi_*\); \(D^{\mathrm{pot}}(z)=z\) almost surely; \(s=+1\); both potential wages take values in the finite grid \(\mathcal Y\); and, for \(EE=\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}\), \(P(EE)\ge m_*>0\).  On this restricted submodel the induced law belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), every unit is a complier, the always-selected-complier event equals \(EE\), and \(M_{\mathrm{ASC}}=P(EE)\).  There is no inclusion of the unrestricted Blanco--Flores--Flores-Lagunes class in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), and their sharpness conclusion does not transfer automatically outside this restriction.

=C_{2/\kappa}\frac{m\log m}{\sqrt n}
+(H_C+A_0)x_n(C)+\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C).

Here \(H_C\) is obtained by finite rational active-set enumeration, and \(\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\) is the explicit Hellinger bound between the score-normal law and \(N_d(u,\Sigma_0)\). \[
\Theta_{\mathrm{ASC}}(p_0)
\subseteq\prod_{t\in\mathcal T}
[\underline\Delta(t;p_0),\overline\Delta(t;p_0)],
\]
with no rectangle-equality claim.  The completed tangent cells define a lawful \(\mathfrak G_0\in\mathfrak E\) with certified nonempty \(H_{r_0}\). \[
M_n^{\diamond}\to M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0),
\qquad
\liminf_nM_n\ge M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
\]
The restricted singleton-\(\mathcal X\), perfect-compliance, finite-wage-grid submodel in \(\text{prop:bffl-discrete-perfect-compliance-embedding}\) embeds the Blanco--Flores--Flores-Lagunes always-employed comparison, but there is no unrestricted-class inclusion or automatic sharpness transfer.
